problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡(2t+1),\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed $|v|$ of the particle at time $t=1.$ Do not round the answer.

The speed at time $t=1$ is
{{field-1}}.

feedback.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1),\,\frac{3}{t}⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed $|v|$ of the particle at time $t=3.$ Do not round the answer.

The speed at time $t=3$ is
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity vector $v.$ Differentiating the position vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{3}{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t+1},\,-\frac{3}{{t}^{2}}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity when $t=3,$ we substitute in the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =⟨\frac{1}{3+1},\,-\frac{3}{{3}^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{4},\,-\frac{1}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the speed at $t=3$ we calculate the magnitude of $v(3),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|v(3)| & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{4})}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{16}+\frac{1}{9}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{25}{144}} \\  & =\frac{5}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$
